_evidence: 0x0053f432 is the item handler (+0x1a) of the twelve static save-slot items 0x8481ce + k*0x26 (ids +0xc 10..21, cells +0xe = 0x7ab1a4 + k*0x40, type +0xd 0, +0x26 = the next item's link); the spec draws esi from exactly those records and ebx (the caller's [item+0xe] cell, 0x53daae/0x53dc57 'mov ebx,[esi+0xe]') as an 8-byte buffer. Command edx = 2 turns ebx into the slot index ('movzx ebx,[esi+0xc]; sub ebx,0xa': 0..11) and then FALLS INTO the command-1 tail, whose equality arm ('mov eax,[0x82fd5a]; cmp al,[0x81e4f8]; jne' then 0x5398c4 'cmp al/ax/eax,[ebx]' for types 0..2) dereferences address 0..11: the original faults whenever command 2 meets that equality (the real items are type 0), so command-2 states with [0x82fd5a].b == the [0x81e4f8].b it leaves are not valid inputs, while command 1 needs the equality to reach 0x5398c4 and the or-arm 0x53f4af. Command 2 leaves [0x81e4f8] = 2 or 0 (slot index == [0x7ab4a4]; slots_007ab1a4 draws both and the slot bytes +0/+0x20) or its input value. Domain: [0x82fd5a] low byte always 1 (high bytes vary); [0x81e4f8] = edx in about half the cases (alias_reg: 1 for command 1 = the equality, 2 for command 2 = never 1), else a value whose low byte is never 1 (command 1 mismatch). So command 1 takes both directions of the 0x53f4a3 'jne', command 2 always the safe one. Item flag bytes +0x1f (RMW 'and 0x7f' / 'or 0x80') any; type bytes +0xd {0,0,1,2,3,0x80} (0x5398c4 uses the low 2 bits: byte/word/dword compare against the valid ebx buffer, 3 = its 'Compare strings?' stub without a dereference).
